title: The Scopes module guards and invokes its own extension inputs
question: The Scopes module's EligibilityBuilder and QueryScopeDirectory use core internals PredicateBuilder, QueryGuard, Narrow, RuntimeInvoker and ModelLookup (i4.json, owner P3). After P3 a module may use only attributed core symbols (I4), and PredicateBuilder/QueryGuard stay core internals because core uses them in ResourceContextMapping and the Relation adapter. How does the module guard and invoke its own extension inputs?

options.text: The module owns the guard of its own SPI inputs: a module-internal narrowing-only builder and guard (Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterQuery, FilterGuard) for filters and access adapters; closure filters are called positionally as AssignmentScopeFilter::apply($query, $runtime) with a compile-time signature check (RuntimeInvoker dropped); Narrow checks inlined; lookup/label helpers as Scopes\Internal\ScopeLookup.
Publish a core Spi(Call) guarded-query factory for modules and third-party evaluators.

context: P3 design session 2026-10-13. Phase P3 scope.exclude forbids exposing internal database mechanisms as public SPI; core already hands eligibleContexts() a guarded group it built itself (D18).
decision: A — The module owns the guard of its own SPI inputs: a module-internal narrowing-only builder and guard (Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterQuery, FilterGuard) for filters and access adapters; closure filters are called positionally as AssignmentScopeFilter::apply($query, $runtime) with a compile-time signature check (RuntimeInvoker dropped); Narrow checks inlined; lookup/label helpers as Scopes\Internal\ScopeLookup.
rationale: No public surface added before the freeze (P3 scope.exclude); each owner guards its own slot inputs; follows D21/D18.
consequences: New module-internal types (not in the P1 oracle; ownership resolved by FQCN per D17): Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterQuery, Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterGuard, Scopes\Internal\ScopeLookup.

Behavior change (migration line): name-injected filter closures (parameters named user, role, grant, actor, panel, scope, now, phase, proposed…) are rejected; use ($query, $runtime) and read the runtime fields.
i4.json loses every EligibilityBuilder and QueryScopeDirectory entry.
